evals.name: codegen-complete-info
evals.prompt:
Add API tests for POST /auth/login. Area folder is app. Treat the following OpenAPI fragment as the documented contract and cover all status codes it lists:

paths:
  /auth/login:
    post:
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [email, password]
              properties:
                email: {type: string}
                password: {type: string}
      responses:
        '200': {description: OK — returns the user object}
        '401': {description: Unauthorized — body has message and statusCode fields}
evals.expected_output: Phase 4 confidence block with score >=8, routes to api-testing first, chains to data-strategy/enums/type-safety, no premature edits, asks human gate before applying.

assertions.text: Output contains a Phase 4 / Proposal block with Confidence: <number>
Confidence score is >=8 (full info, low risk)
Both Rationale and Unknowns lines present in proposal
References api-testing skill as first skill loaded
Stops to await human approval before generating any test files
Does not invent new folder names or file paths beyond what user supplied or what ls would reveal

evals.name: codegen-missing-area
evals.prompt: Add tests for the login API endpoint.
evals.expected_output: Asks the user for area folder + spec source. Does NOT emit Phase 4 with confidence <5, does NOT invent front-office or any area name.

assertions.text: Output contains an explicit question to the user about area folder, endpoint path, or spec source
Does NOT emit a full Phase 4 Proposal block (per <5 -> ASK rule)
Does not name a specific area folder (front-office / back-office / portal) without user input
Does not start writing test code, schemas, or factories
References the <5 -> ASK rule, missing-input rule, or equivalent reason for asking

evals.name: codegen-missing-source
evals.prompt: Test the user signup endpoint. It returns 201 on success.
evals.expected_output: Asks for OpenAPI / Swagger source first. Does NOT jump to live HTTP exploration. Does NOT invent endpoint path, request body shape, or response schema.

assertions.text: Asks for OpenAPI / Swagger documentation location before doing anything else
Does not assume a specific endpoint path like /api/users or /api/signup without confirmation
Does not invent field names for the signup request body
If proposing live HTTP, frames it as fallback for when no spec exists, not the primary approach
Does not emit a full Phase 4 Proposal block before getting the spec source

evals.name: refactor-cascading-rename
evals.prompt: Rename the value of ApiEndpoints.LOGIN from /auth/login to /v2/auth/login.
evals.expected_output: Loads refactor-values skill, runs impact-grep across enums/, fixtures/, tests/, helpers/ before proposing edits. Phase 4 includes affected file list as evidence.

assertions.text: References or loads the refactor-values skill
Performs an impact analysis (grep / search) for ApiEndpoints.LOGIN call sites BEFORE proposing edits
Phase 4 Proposal lists the files that will change, not just the enum file
Does not edit the enum value without first showing impact
Considers or asks about test-data/static/ files that may hardcode the path

evals.name: debug-flaky-test
evals.prompt: This test is flaky in CI: tests/app/api/login.spec.ts. It passes locally but fails about 1 in 5 runs in CI with a TimeoutError — the POST to ApiEndpoints.LOGIN times out before a response arrives. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Loads debugging skill. Investigates root cause via trace/CI artifacts. Does NOT bump timeouts. Does NOT add page.waitForTimeout. Distinguishes test bug vs product bug. Considers test.skip + FIXME if confirmed product bug.

assertions.text: References or loads the debugging skill
Does NOT propose raising timeout values or adding test.setTimeout to mask the failure
Does NOT propose page.waitForTimeout or any hard wait
Proposes pulling CI traces / screenshots / videos before patching
If pointing toward a product bug, considers test.skip + // FIXME instead of silent failure or weakening assertion

evals.name: ui-explore-no-cli
evals.prompt: Create a page object for the /admin page. By the way, playwright-cli is not installed and I cannot install it right now. Can you use the IDE browser MCP to explore the page instead?
evals.expected_output: Refuses to substitute another tool for playwright-cli. Cites No Substitute UI Exploration WON'T rule. Stops and asks the user to install playwright-cli or supply the page structure.

assertions.text: Refuses to use IDE browser MCP / Cursor browser / playwright codegen as substitute for playwright-cli
Cites the No Substitute UI Exploration rule or the Explore Before Generate MUST
Does not produce a page object with invented locators
Asks user to install playwright-cli or supply page structure manually

evals.name: direct-mode-trivial
evals.prompt: There's a typo in the JSDoc of enums/util/roles.ts -- it says 'shraed across all application areas' instead of 'shared'. Just fix it.
evals.expected_output: Direct Mode routing: no full Phase 4 ritual for a one-word typo. Opens the file first; the outcome must match what the file actually contains (fix if the typo exists, report the mismatch if it doesn't). Graded on mode selection, not on whether the premise holds.

assertions.text: Handles the request in Direct Mode -- no full 8-phase ritual or Proposal/Confidence/Rationale/Unknowns block for a one-word typo
Opens enums/util/roles.ts and checks the cited JSDoc before editing

Outcome is consistent with the file's actual content: applies the one-word fix if the typo exists, otherwise reports that the cited typo is not present -- never edits something else to satisfy the request
Does not bundle unrelated cleanup or refactors

evals.name: direct-mode-false-premise
evals.prompt: There's a typo in fixtures/pom/test-options.ts on line 1 -- the comment says 'Singel import point'. Just fix it.
evals.expected_output: Opens the file, finds the premise is false (no such typo on line 1), stops and reports the mismatch instead of applying any edit.

assertions.text: Reads the cited file/line before editing
Reports that the described typo does not exist at the cited location
Does not modify the file or 'fix' something else to satisfy the request
Asks the user to re-check or clarifies what they meant instead of guessing

evals.name: confidence-band-5-7-tradeoff
evals.prompt:
Add API tests for DELETE /api/sessions/:id. Area folder is app. The documented contract is exactly this OpenAPI fragment -- it documents 204 (deleted) and 401 (unauthorized) but says nothing about what happens for a non-existent session id; the team thinks it's 404 but nobody is sure:

paths:
  /api/sessions/{id}:
    delete:
      responses:
        '204': {description: Deleted}
        '401': {description: Unauthorized}

Proceed with what you have.
evals.expected_output: Emits Phase 4 with confidence in the 5-7 band, the 404 ambiguity listed under Unknowns, and waits for the human to accept the trade-off. Does not silently assume 404 is documented, does not refuse outright.

assertions.text: Emits a Phase 4 Proposal block with a confidence score in the 5-7 range
The undocumented non-existent-id behavior appears explicitly in the Unknowns line
Waits for human confirmation before applying, framing the unknown as an accepted trade-off decision
Plans to cover the ambiguous case via test.skip + FIXME or flags it for spec clarification -- not silently omitted

evals.name: rejection-reenters-phase3
evals.prompt: Earlier you proposed adding login API tests built on the spec export I gave you, and I rejected the plan because that export is outdated -- the real contract is the v2 spec the backend team publishes. Continue.
evals.expected_output: Re-enters Phase 3 with the stated gap: asks where the v2 spec lives. Does NOT re-emit the same plan against docs/openapi.yml.

assertions.text: Does not re-propose the same plan built on the rejected spec export
Asks where the v2 spec lives (URL / file / export) before planning again
Frames the next step as renewed exploration (Phase 3) with the stated gap, not as a defense of the rejected plan

evals.name: routing-factory-data-strategy
evals.prompt: Create a factory for generating product test data -- products have a name, a price, and a category. Area folder is app.
evals.expected_output: Routes to data-strategy as first skill, chains to type-safety, plans a Faker+Zod factory under test-data/factories/app/, does not put dynamic data in test-data/static/.

assertions.text: References data-strategy as the first skill loaded
Plans the factory under test-data/factories/app/ with a .factory.ts name
Uses Faker for the generated values, not hardcoded strings
Does not place dynamic happy-path data under test-data/static/

evals.name: routing-env-var-config
evals.prompt: Our tests need to hit a new reporting service. Add a REPORTING_URL environment variable and make it available to tests.
evals.expected_output: Routes to config as first skill: declares the var in env/.env.example, adds a config property with JSDoc naming the env var, does not put the URL in an enum or hardcode it.

assertions.text: References the config skill as the routing target
Plans to declare REPORTING_URL in env/.env.example
Does not put the URL into enums/ (URLs are env/config, not enums)
Config property JSDoc names the backing env variable

evals.name: headless-gate-policy
evals.prompt:
You are running non-interactively (claude -p, no human available to answer). Add API tests for POST /auth/login. Area folder is app. Treat the following OpenAPI fragment as the documented contract and cover all status codes it lists:

paths:
  /auth/login:
    post:
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              required: [email, password]
              properties:
                email: {type: string}
                password: {type: string}
      responses:
        '200': {description: OK — returns the user object}
        '401': {description: Unauthorized — body has message and statusCode fields}
evals.expected_output: All primary inputs present -> confidence >=8 with Unknowns: none -> may auto-proceed through Phase 5, and the final report explicitly states the human gate was auto-passed and why. If anything is unknown, emits the proposal and stops instead.

assertions.text: References the non-interactive Phase 5 policy (auto-proceed only at confidence >=8 with no unknowns)
If proceeding, the report states the human gate was auto-passed and on what grounds
If any unknown or sub-8 confidence exists, emits the proposal as final output and stops instead of applying
